title: Case 1: Recruitment & Conditions of Service of Public Servants (Article 309 • Writ Petition)
legalTheme: Part XIV: Services under the Union and the States • Article 309
factualMatrix: Before the Supreme Court of India (Article 32), an aggrieved petitioner challenged an impugned executive notification and enforcement order issued by the Union Ministry / Central Authority under Article 309 (Recruitment & Conditions of Service of Public Servants) of Part XIV (Services under the Union and the States). Relying on the core guarantee that Empowers Parliament and State Legislatures to regulate the recruitment and conditions of service of public servants, authorizing the President and Governors to frame service rules until legislative acts are enacted. and citing Union of India v. Tulsiram Patel (1985), the petitioner sought judicial invalidation for violating constitutional limits and procedural fairness.
framingQuestions: 1. Whether the Writ Petition before the Supreme Court of India (Article 32) is maintainable under Article 309?
2. Does the Union Ministry / Central Authority's executive notification and enforcement order conform to Article 309 (Recruitment & Conditions of Service of Public Servants)?
3. How does Union of India v. Tulsiram Patel (1985) govern the constitutional validity and relief in this matter?
statutoryApplicability: Union of India v. Tulsiram Patel (1985)
modelAnswer:
1. MAINTAINABILITY: The Writ Petition before the Supreme Court of India (Article 32) is maintainable as it raises a direct constitutional question under Article 309 (Part XIV).

2. SUBSTANTIVE ANALYSIS (Article 309): Empowers Parliament and State Legislatures to regulate the recruitment and conditions of service of public servants, authorizing the President and Governors to frame service rules until legislative acts are enacted. Applying the governing principle—'Doctrine of Pleasure (Art 310): Civil servants hold office during the pleasure of the President or Governor.'—the impugned executive notification and enforcement order by the Union Ministry / Central Authority must strictly satisfy constitutional bounds.

3. PRECEDENT (Union of India v. Tulsiram Patel (1985)) & RELIEF: Guided by Union of India v. Tulsiram Patel (1985), any overreach inconsistent with Article 309 is liable to be quashed or suitably restrained.

markingRubric.criterion: Precedent reasoning (Union of India v. Tulsiram Patel (1985)) & relief

factualMatrix: A constitutional question arose before the Administrative / Statutory Tribunal concerning the scope of Article 311 (Dismissal, Removal & Reduction in Rank (The Twin Civil Service Shields)) under Part XIV (Services under the Union and the States). While the District Collector / Executive Magistrate invoked broad administrative discretion, the petitioner relied on Union of India v. Tulsiram Patel (1985) and the principle that Article 312: Rajya Sabha has unique federal power to create new All-India Services by 2/3 resolution., requiring the Bench to determine maintainability, statutory compliance, and appropriate relief.
